name: manual_cdd062
claim: When a client-side auth resolver picks 'the one preferred token' (e.g. candidates[0] of a priority list) and a peer/service rejects it, don't conclude the credential isn't deployed -- test every LOCALLY AVAILABLE candidate directly against the target first. In a real incident, a second local token candidate was accepted (HTTP 200) by the exact service that rejected the first one; the fix was retrying across candidates client-side, not an operator syncing anything. Single-token resolvers used for AUTHENTICATION should retry across all available candidates on 401/403 before surfacing an operator-actionable error, mirroring how multi-candidate retry is already used elsewhere in the same codebase for exactly this reason.

decisions.notes: Two call sites (a topology-query script and a peer-file-drop script) each called a single-token resolver instead of the multi-candidate list a THIRD script in the same file already used successfully. Cost one full investigation cycle (correctly-worded but wrong root-cause finding, self-corrected) before the real bug (client retry gap, not token deployment) was found by directly testing each candidate.
